# pm-facing_alias: # Schema: PM-facing alias, wire-format model id, reasoning effort.
# This file is the codex adapter alias table. The claude adapter alias table
# lives at share/claude-model-aliases.tsv (same 3-column format).
# Columns must be tab-separated.
# Executor-agnostic alias — use in briefs, PM routing, and dispatch policy docs:
#   `light`  — lightweight/fast model for targeted changes (< 50 lines, ≤ 2 files,
#              no new behavioral units). Mapped per executor:
#                codex  → codex-spark (gpt-5.3-codex-spark, independent pool, ~64K ctx)
#                claude → haiku       (claude-haiku-4-5, see claude-model-aliases.tsv)
# GPT 5.6 ships as three named variants (not a single `gpt-5.6` id):
#   gpt-5.6-sol    — latest frontier agentic coding model
#   gpt-5.6-terra  — balanced agentic coding model for everyday work
#   gpt-5.6-luna   — fast and affordable agentic coding model
# Default model: pm-dispatch pins its OWN default model (gpt-5.6-terra, see
# DEFAULT_DISPATCH_MODEL in adapters/codex/dispatch.sh), decoupled from the
# user's interactive ~/.codex/config.toml `model` setting. Omitting --model
# therefore dispatches on gpt-5.6-terra — NOT whatever the local codex config
# defaults to. Override per-host via ~/.pm-dispatch/config `dispatch.default_model`.
#   gpt-5.6-terra  — primary default (balanced/everyday tier)
#   gpt-5.5        — fallback (set dispatch.default_model = gpt-5.5 if gpt-5.6-terra is unavailable)
#   gpt-5.4        — second fallback (set dispatch.default_model = gpt-5.4 if both above are unavailable)
# `gpt-5.6-sol` (frontier) and `gpt-5.6-luna` (fast/affordable) are available as
# explicit aliases for callers who want to name a tier directly — neither is
# the default; see docs/model-tier-policy.md for when to reach for the
# frontier tier.
# `codex-spark` / `light` draw from an INDEPENDENT usage pool and are opt-in only
# (PM routes here for known-small changes — see agents/project-pm.md); never default.
# Context window reference:
#   light / codex-spark  — gpt-5.3-codex-spark  ~64K tokens
#   gpt-5.6-terra         — ~122K+ tokens (default; same tier as prior gpt-5.5)
# Survey-style briefs that read large files MUST use lazy-read instructions.
# Reasoning effort: an alias's effort column is the practical default whenever
# `--effort` is omitted (it takes precedence over the global default — see
# scripts/lib/reasoning-effort.sh). default/gpt-5.6-*/gpt-5.5/gpt-5.4 converge
# to medium so a plain dispatch/gate call is medium by default without needing
# `--effort medium` on every invocation; codex-spark/light stay high,
# unchanged and orthogonal to this convergence (their small-model/low-latency
# tuning is a separate concern from reasoning depth).
default
gpt-5.6-terra
gpt-5.6-sol
gpt-5.6-luna
gpt-5.5
gpt-5.4
codex-spark
light
